Taxonomy

Source: vignettes/articles/taxonomy.Rmd
taxonomy.Rmd

Every title that titleclassifier codes ends up described along four dimensions:

Dimension Columns Set by Answers
Standard title title.standard crosswalk, step 07 which title is this, spelled one way?
Domain and occupation domain.category, domain.label, SOC codes taxonomy, step 08 what area of work is it in?
Level or board role emp.level or board.role (title only); role.final, role.board, role.ceo (resolved) taxonomy, step 08; rules and model, step 09 how senior is the person, and are they staff or board?
Qualifiers strata, strata.label, status flags, multiple-title fields crosswalk, steps 04, 06 and 07 rank within the title, status in the role, other roles held

The standard titles and their taxonomy are package data: get_title_taxonomy() returns one row per standard title (450 titles), and get_title_xwalk() maps the 9,181 known variants onto them.

Domains

The domain says what area of an organization the title works in. It has two levels: four broad categories, plus a fifth for entries that are not job titles, and a label within each category.

domain.category Meaning
executive top staff leadership and general management
governance board members and board officers
operations support functions found in any organization: finance, fundraising, HR, technology, …
industry-specific work specific to the organization’s field: medical, education, religion, …
non-job title no title, boilerplate in place of one, or text that is not a job

The source of the domain vocabulary is data-raw/crosswalks/domains.csv.

Occupation codes (SOC)

Job titles carry a 2018 BLS Standard Occupational Classification code at four levels: major.group (two digits), minor.group, broad.group and detailed.occupation, with the occupation’s name in soc.label. Board seats have no SOC code: serving on a board is not an occupation.

major.group titles occupations
11 186 Sales Managers, Chief Executives, Lodging Managers
13 35 Fundraisers, Loan Officers, Compliance Officers
15 3 Actuaries, Web Developers, Computer Occupations
17 2 Architects, Except Naval
19 5 Historians, Life, Physical, and Social Science Occupations
21 14 Clergy, Counselors, Religious Workers, All Other
23 7 Lawyers, Legal Support Workers, All Other
25 23 Curators, Archivists, Postsecondary Teachers
27 40 Actors, Editors, Art Directors
29 10 Surgeons, Paramedics, Physicians
33 5 Firefighters, Security Guards, First-Line Supervisors of Security Workers
35 3 Bartenders, Chefs and Head Cooks
37 4 Janitors and Cleaners, Except Maids and Housekeeping Cleaners, First-Line Supervisors of Landscaping, Lawn Service, and Groundskeeping Workers
39 1 Tour Guides and Escorts
41 2 First-Line Supervisors of Retail Sales Workers, Sales Representatives of Services, Except Advertising, Insurance, Financial Services, and Travel
43 14 Dispatchers, Office Clerks, General, Secretaries and Administrative Assistants
49 2 Maintenance and Repair Workers, General, Electrical Power-Line Installers and Repairers
53 1 Commercial Pilots

Most leadership titles fall in major group 11, Management Occupations.

Roles

A person’s role is the central output. It has two forms:

  • Title only (step 08): the taxonomy gives each standard title either an employee level (emp.level) or a board role (board.role), never both. This is what the title says on its own.
  • Resolved (step 09): role.final is the role after reading the filer’s checkboxes, pay and hours. A PRESIDENT is a board seat by title, but a paid, full-time president with no other CEO is the CEO. See step 09.

Employee levels

Level Who Example titles
CEO the top staff job; one person per filing, or co-CEOs CEO, CO-CEO, PASTOR, PRESIDENT
OFFICER C-suite below the CEO, vice presidents, deputies, general counsel CAO, CFO, CMO, COO
MANAGER directors of departments and managers DEAN, CAPTAIN, FOREMAN, MANAGER
PROFESSIONAL highly paid non-managerial experts: physicians, lawyers, professors, coaches ACTOR, COACH, NURSE, PILOT
STAFF everyone else on staff: counselors, chefs, teachers, assistants CHEF, IMAM, CLERK, ELDER 
table(tax$emp.level[tax$emp.level != ""])
#> 
#>          CEO      MANAGER      OFFICER PROFESSIONAL        STAFF 
#>           11          129          139           40          116

Board roles

Board role Standard title Variants include
CHAIR BOARD PRESIDENT CHAIR, CHAIRMAN, CHAIRPERSON, PRESIDENT (unpaid)
VICE CHAIR BOARD VICE PRESIDENT VICE CHAIR, VICE PRESIDENT (on the board)
SECRETARY BOARD SECRETARY SECRETARY, CLERK, ADJUTANT
TREASURER BOARD TREASURER TREASURER
MEMBER BOARD MEMBER DIRECTOR, TRUSTEE, GOVERNOR, COMMITTEE MEMBER, …

When step 09 turns an employee title into a board seat (an unpaid VICE PRESIDENT who ticks only the trustee box, say), role.board is read from the title: VICE PRESIDENT becomes VICE CHAIR.

Resolved role columns

Column Values Meaning
role.final CEO, OFFICER, MANAGER, PROFESSIONAL, STAFF, BOARD the person’s role
role.board CHAIR, VICE CHAIR, SECRETARY, TREASURER, MEMBER for BOARD: the seat; for a person with several board titles, the most senior
role.ceo designated, co-ceo, interim, imputed, model for CEO: how the CEO was found. designated: a CEO-level title in an officer position. co-ceo: two or more designated. interim: designated and flagged interim. imputed: no CEO title, the highest-paid plausible leader. model: named by the 990-EZ model
role.position board, officer, board_officer, staff, unknown the position from the checkboxes (or title and pay)
role.source checkbox, title+pay, title what settled the position
role.method rules, model which classifier decided (Rules and models)
org.leadership designated, imputed, model, board_governed, no_paid per filing: how its chief executive was found. board_governed: people are paid but none is a plausible leader. no_paid: nobody is paid

Strata

The crosswalk drops rank and type words from the standard title and records them in strata and strata.label, so that SENIOR VICE PRESIDENT OF MARKETING and VICE PRESIDENT OF MARKETING share one standard but stay distinguishable.

strata Meaning strata.label values
superior a higher rank of the title head, chair, chief, grand, senior, exalted, general, leading, managing, executive, executive senior
subordinate a lower rank of the title vice, deputy, junior, advisory, assistant, associate
duplex a second kind of seat alongside the usual one co, adhoc, advisory, at large, emeritus, honorary, alternate, exofficio
committee a committee seat, and which committee hr, vp, chair, member, finance, lifetime, executive, marketing, management, supervisory
regional a regional version of the title regional
exofficio a seat held by virtue of another office exofficio 
table(xwalk$strata[xwalk$strata != ""])
#> 
#>   committee      duplex   exofficio    regional   regional? subordinate 
#>         278         138           1         192           1         209 
#>    superior 
#>         358
head(xwalk[xwalk$strata == "superior", ], 6)
#>         title.variant   title.standard   strata strata.label
#> 773       BOARD CHAIR  BOARD PRESIDENT superior        chair
#> 1403     CHIEF ACCOUN CHIEF ACCOUNTANT superior        chief
#> 1404 CHIEF ACCOUNTANT CHIEF ACCOUNTANT superior        chief
#> 1417  CHIEF ARCHITECT  CHIEF ARCHITECT superior        chief
#> 1430        CHIEF CEO              CEO superior        chief
#> 1432      CHIEF CLERK      CHIEF CLERK superior        chief

Status flags

Step 06 removes status qualifiers from the title and records each as a 0/1 flag. A person’s flags apply to all of their titles.

Flag Set when the title says Examples
former.x the person has left the role FORMER, PAST, EMERITUS, RETIRED
interim.x the role is temporary INTERIM, ACTING, TEMPORARY
future.x the person started during the year or will start ELECT, INCOMING, SINCE, EFFECTIVE
outgoing.x the person left during the year OUTGOING, THRU, UNTIL, RESIGNED, TERM ENDED
partial.x part of the year only: a date, or outgoing, future or partial-year status PARTIAL YEAR, PART YEAR
founder.x the person founded the organization FOUNDER, CO-FOUNDER
ex.officio.x the seat comes with another office EX OFFICIO
at.large.x a seat not tied to a constituency AT LARGE, AS NEEDED, PROXY
co.x the role is shared CO-CHAIR, CO-DIRECTOR
region.x the role covers a region or chapter REGIONAL, CHAPTER, DISTRICT, state and city names
sched.o.x the filer pointed to Schedule O instead of a title SEE SCHEDULE O
date.x the title contained a date (step 02) (THRU 6/2023), 2021-2023

The status crosswalk lists every spelling of each status:

table(sc$status.qualifier)

#>         5         1         4        14         4        30         6        33 
#>   PARTIAL  REGIONAL   SCHED O 
#>        10       182         5
head(sc[sc$status.qualifier == "FUTURE", ], 8)
#>    status.variant status.qualifier
#> 29          AFTER           FUTURE
#> 30            BEG           FUTURE
#> 31          BEGAN           FUTURE
#> 32           BEGI           FUTURE
#> 33          BEGIN           FUTURE
#> 34      BEGINNING           FUTURE
#> 35            EFF           FUTURE
#> 36      EFFECTIVE           FUTURE

People with several roles

A Part VII entry can name several roles, and a person can sit on the board and work on staff. These are recorded at three levels:

  • Several titles in one entry. “PRESIDENT & TREASURER” becomes two rows (step 04). title.count is the person’s number of titles, title.order this title’s position, and title.mult.x marks people with more than one. Both rows carry the person’s pay and hours once; the per-filing counts (num.dtk, num.board, …) weight them so that the person is counted once.
  • One role per person. Step 09 resolves each person to a single role.final, using their most senior position, and marks one of their rows with role.primary = TRUE. Count people with role.primary; count titles without it.
  • Dual roles. A person who ticks both the trustee and officer boxes holds a board seat and an office (role.position = "board_officer"). They are BOARD unless paid in an executive title, in which case they are CEO or OFFICER: a working board member who runs the organization.
  • Shared roles. co.x marks a shared title (CO-CHAIR). Two or more designated CEOs in a filing are each role.ceo = "co-ceo".
data(tinypartvii)
set.seed(3)
df <- dplyr::sample_n(tinypartvii, 400) |>
  standardize_df() |> remove_dates() |> standardize_conj() |> split_titles() |>
  standardize_spelling() |> gen_status_codes() |> standardize_titles() |>
  categorize_titles() |> conditional_logic()
#> [OK] standardize df step complete
#> [OK] remove dates step complete
#> [OK] standardize conjunctions step complete
#> [OK] split titles step complete
#> [OK] standardize spelling step complete
#> [OK] generate status codes step complete
#> [OK] standardize titles step complete
#> [OK] categorize titles step complete
#> 
#> [OK] conditional logic step complete
multi <- df[df$title.count > 1, c("dtk.name", "title.raw", "title.standard", "title.order",
                                  "role.position", "role.final", "role.primary")]
head(multi[order(multi$dtk.name, multi$title.order), ], 8)
#>            dtk.name                           title.raw
#> 236   AMIEE L SMITH                  PRESIDENT/DIRECTOR
#> 237   AMIEE L SMITH                  PRESIDENT/DIRECTOR
#> 3   Austin Woodruff President and Chairman of the Board
#> 4   Austin Woodruff President and Chairman of the Board
#> 232 DEBBIE WILLIAMS                  EXECUTIVE VP & COO
#> 233 DEBBIE WILLIAMS                  EXECUTIVE VP & COO
#> 364 James B Pieffer              Director and President
#> 365 James B Pieffer              Director and President
#>               title.standard title.order role.position role.final role.primary
#> 236          BOARD PRESIDENT           1         board      BOARD         TRUE
#> 237             BOARD MEMBER           2         board      BOARD        FALSE
#> 3            BOARD PRESIDENT           1         staff        CEO         TRUE
#> 4            BOARD PRESIDENT           2         staff        CEO        FALSE
#> 232 EXECUTIVE VICE PRESIDENT           1       officer        CEO         TRUE
#> 233  CHIEF OPERATING OFFICER           2       officer        CEO        FALSE
